Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects: testReuseOptionsTwice builds an Options with a single required option -v, parses once with "-v" (should succeed), then reuses the same Options instance to parse an empty argument list (should throw MissingOptionException because the required -v is missing).

- Observed failure: The second parse does not throw MissingOptionException.

- Relevant code path:
  - Parser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean) starts by “clearing out the data in options in case it’s been used before,” but only clears option values via:
    for (Iterator it = options.helpOptions().iterator(); it.hasNext();) {
        Option opt = (Option) it.next();
        opt.clearValues();
    }
  - It then calls setOptions(options), initializes a new CommandLine, parses tokens, and finally calls checkRequiredOptions().
  - checkRequiredOptions() throws MissingOptionException only if getRequiredOptions().size() > 0.

- Root cause: Required-option state is being shared and mutated across parses.
  - During the first parse, when the required option -v is encountered, the parser removes it from its tracking list of required options. If Parser’s requiredOptions list is not a fresh copy but instead directly references Options’ internal required options list (or if processOption removes from Options’ list), then the Options object ends up permanently losing -v from its “required options” set.
  - On the second parse with the same Options instance, setOptions(options) initializes required-options tracking from a list that is already missing -v, so getRequiredOptions().size() is 0 and checkRequiredOptions() does not throw.

- Why this matches the test and report:
  - The test only fails when reusing the same Options instance, which is exactly when shared mutable state in Options would affect subsequent parses.
  - The current parse() method resets option values but does not reset the required-options tracking within Options; if Parser aliases Options’ required list (instead of copying), or if processOption removes from Options’ list, the subsequent parse incorrectly sees no required options remaining.
  - This aligns with the bug report: “When an Options object is used to parse a second set of command arguments it won’t throw a MissingOptionException.”

- Conclusion: There is an aliasing/state-leak bug in how the parser manages required options across parses. The parser should maintain its own per-parse copy of the required options and mutate only that copy, leaving Options’ internal required options intact.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

m21.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects: testReuseOptionsTwice builds an Options with a single required option -v, parses once with "-v" (should succeed), then reuses the same Options instance to parse an empty argument list (should throw MissingOptionException because the required -v is missing).

- Observed failure: The second parse does not throw MissingOptionException.

- Relevant code path:
  - Parser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean) starts by “clearing out the data in options in case it’s been used before,” but only clears option values via:
    for (Iterator it = options.helpOptions().iterator(); it.hasNext();) {
        Option opt = (Option) it.next();
        opt.clearValues();
    }
  - It then calls setOptions(options), initializes a new CommandLine, parses tokens, and finally calls checkRequiredOptions().
  - checkRequiredOptions() throws MissingOptionException only if getRequiredOptions().size() > 0.

- Root cause: Required-option state is being shared and mutated across parses.
  - During the first parse, when the required option -v is encountered, the parser removes it from its tracking list of required options. If Parser’s requiredOptions list is not a fresh copy but instead directly references Options’ internal required options list (or if processOption removes from Options’ list), then the Options object ends up permanently losing -v from its “required options” set.
  - On the second parse with the same Options instance, setOptions(options) initializes required-options tracking from a list that is already missing -v, so getRequiredOptions().size() is 0 and checkRequiredOptions() does not throw.

- Why this matches the test and report:
  - The test only fails when reusing the same Options instance, which is exactly when shared mutable state in Options would affect subsequent parses.
  - The current parse() method resets option values but does not reset the required-options tracking within Options; if Parser aliases Options’ required list (instead of copying), or if processOption removes from Options’ list, the subsequent parse incorrectly sees no required options remaining.
  - This aligns with the bug report: “When an Options object is used to parse a second set of command arguments it won’t throw a MissingOptionException.”

- Conclusion: There is an aliasing/state-leak bug in how the parser manages required options across parses. The parser should maintain its own per-parse copy of the required options and mutate only that copy, leaving Options’ internal required options intact.
